name: Pineal Tumor of Neuroepithelial Tissue

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System

criteria.description: Histopathological confirmation of neuroepithelial tumor cells in pineal region
MRI showing a mass localized to the pineal gland with characteristic signal intensities
Positive staining for neuronal and glial markers (e.g., synaptophysin, GFAP)
Symptoms consistent with pineal region mass effect such as Parinaud syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus characteristic imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular profiling may assist in tumor subclassification and prognosis.

searchTerms: difficulty moving eyes up and down

pathognomonic.symptomName: Obstructive hydrocephalus due to aqueductal compression
searchTerms: brain fluid blockage from narrow passage
hydrocephalus due to brain channel compression

common.symptomName: Headache secondary to increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: head pain due to increased intracranial pressure

common.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting related to intracranial hypertension
searchTerms: nausea caused by increased head pressure

common.symptomName: Diplopia due to cranial nerve involvement
common.notes: Often related to impaired ocular motility

searchTerms: unsteady walking due to brain pathway damage

occasional.notes: Due to involvement of adjacent structures
May result from optic pathway compression

occasional.symptomName: Endocrine disturbances such as precocious puberty
occasional.notes: Rarely caused by pineal gland dysfunction
Due to pineal gland involvement affecting melatonin secretion

rare.notes: Uncommon but possible with cortical irritation

rare.symptomName: Parinaud’s dorsal midbrain syndrome with pupillary light-near dissociation
searchTerms: eye movement and pupil reaction problems
difficulty with pupil light response and gaze

laboratory: CSF analysis typically non-specific but may exclude infection
Tumor markers (AFP, β-hCG) usually negative distinguishing from germ cell tumors
imaging: MRI showing well-demarcated pineal region mass with heterogeneous enhancement
Hydrocephalus due to aqueductal stenosis visible on MRI
genetic: Molecular alterations may include mutations in DICER1, RB1, or other neuroepithelial tumor-associated genes
other: Histopathology demonstrating neuroepithelial differentiation with immunohistochemical positivity for neuronal and glial markers

distinguishingFeatures: Elevated serum or CSF tumor markers (AFP, β-hCG)
Different histopathological profile with germ cell elements
Well-differentiated pineal parenchymal tumor with less aggressive behavior
More aggressive clinical course and different molecular markers

redFlags: Sudden onset of vertical gaze palsy
Signs of increased intracranial pressure such as papilledema
references: Louis DN, Perry A, Reifenberger G, et al. The 2021 WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System: a summary. Neuro Oncol. 2021.
Orphanet: Pineal tumor of neuroepithelial tissue - ORPHA:251905
Kleihues P, Cavenee WK. Pathology and Genetics of Tumors of the Nervous System. IARC Press; 2000.
